thread:
mike: heads-up, hit a weird outage in eu-west edge after the GPU fleet scaled this morning, several services backed by headless svc returned 502/connection refused from our LB. looks like endpoints were being marked notReady intermittently.
anika: timeline? was there an autoscaler event or deploy?
mike: autoscaler added nodes at ~05:42 UTC, errors started ~05:48. sre-bot shows scale event.
sre-bot: autoscaler: scaled_up 4 nodes (reason: pod_pending_pressure) at 2026-03-18T05:42:10Z
jihoon: can you paste outputs: `kubectl get endpointslices -n edge -l app=my-worker -o wide` and `kubectl get endpoints -n edge svc/my-worker -o yaml` - want to check slices vs endpoints sync
mike: pasted below:
```
# endpointslices
NAME                          ADDRESS_TYPE   ENDPOINTS   AGE
my-worker-7xkq2             IPv4           0           2m
my-worker-2m9jf             IPv4           4           11m

# endpoints
apiVersion: v1
kind: Endpoints
metadata:
  name: my-worker
subsets:
  - addresses: []
    notReadyAddresses:
      - ip: 10.4.12.77
        nodeName: ip-10-1-4-77
      - ip: 10.4.12.78
        nodeName: ip-10-1-4-78
```
anika: endpoints object shows only notReadyAddresses but pods appear healthy when exec'ing into them. weird.
vlad: this smells like node-level networking/NAT or conntrack. LB health checks hitting node IPs might be getting SNATed and exhausting ephemeral ports during the spike. check `conntrack -S` and NAT stats on the nodes hosting pods.
mike: checked conntrack, entries near limit on two nodes: nf_conntrack_count ~ 950k of 1M. SYN backlog spiked during scale.
jihoon: also note we still have some nodes running kube-proxy in iptables mode instead of ipvs in that AZ - ipvs would handle many more concurrent endpoints. what does `kubectl get ds kube-proxy -n kube-system -o yaml` show for those tainted nodes?
mike: older kube-proxy image pinned on the problematic AZ. can roll.
anika: suggested mitigations: 1) bump conntrack max on AMI for edge nodes, 2) finish kube-proxy ipvs rollout for whole fleet, 3) introduce small delay/throttle in autoscaler to avoid cold conntrack storms when many nodes join quickly, 4) add runbook entry for headless svc + LB healthcheck interactions.
vlad: also consider tuning conntrack TCP timeouts and enabling listen socket reuse for health checks on LB side so ephemeral port reuse is better.
mike: did a temporary sysctl bump on two affected nodes: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000` and `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=1800` - conntrack dropped from ~95% to ~40% and endpoints stabilized (endpoints object shows addresses populated again).
anika: any CoreDNS involvement? logs showed some SERVFAILs while the nodes were overloaded which caused some clients to re-query and cache inconsistent SRV ordering. TTL=30s so should self-heal but coupled with healthcheck churn caused ~2m of 502s.
jihoon: action items (short): [1] bake conntrack defaults into edge AMI, [2] complete kube-proxy ipvs rollout and ensure no nodes left on iptables, [3] autoscaler backoff tweak to limit concurrent node additions, [4] add runbook and postmortem in INF ticket, [5] consider LB healthcheck config to reuse connections/ports.
sre-bot: ticket created: INF-3241 "eu-west edge: headless endpoints flapping after GPU scale-up"
mike: after the temporary fixes and rolling kube-proxy on the AZ, traffic recovered and error rates returned to baseline. I'll update INF-3241 with logs and commands.
anika: thanks for the quick triage :thumbsup:
